specialRules.ruleFull: The warband's Swabbies are human, and are captured rather than hired, under the Sartosa campaign rules.
The warband hires Hired Swords and buys other items as a human Mercenary warband does. A warband holding both Dwarfs and Elves pays 20 gold crowns more in upkeep.
Unlike other Pirate warbands, the Sartosans may start with a Swivel Gun, bought as normal. In a one-off game they start with two free Swabbies.
If the Captain is killed, one of the Mates takes his place, as a Champion does in a Mercenary warband.
Any pirate within 6" of the Captain may use his Leadership for any Leadership test.

A Gunner carrying the Swivel Gun always counts as an individual and may never be joined by anyone else. Since the warband may hold only one Swivel Gun, the Gunner carrying it is either newly hired or split off from his group, keeping the experience and skills he had.

fighters.name: Boatswain
fighters.equipment: A Rope & Hook, which he may never sell or give away.

specialRules.ruleFull: A Boatswain may re-roll a failed Initiative test for leaping over a gap, jumping down or making a diving charge, and the test for climbing up or down with a rope.
Swabbies are not hired: they are captured, under the Sartosa campaign rules.
Swabbies need not be armed alike: each may carry different equipment, but only from the Swabbie Equipment list. A Swabbie may never use magic or cast a spell.
If the warband routs, any Swabbie who has already left the table in an earlier turn escapes for good: remove him from the roster as if he had been killed.

specialRules.rulename: 'Don't mind them mates, they ain't true pirates!'
specialRules.ruleFull: Swabbies who are running away or have been taken out of action do not count towards the warband's rout test.

rules.name: Blackpowder
rules.text: A natural 1 to hit is a misfire: roll on the Blackpowder misfire table. On a BOOM result the wielder suffers 1D3+1 Strength 3 hits. It may be used with Superior Blackpowder, which makes a BOOM's hits Strength 4.

rules.name: Spread-Shot
rules.text: When a shot in the shooting phase hits, the closest 1D3 models within 2" of the target are hit too, the closest first, with no armour save modifier. The firer is never hit and never counts as the closest model, but his own warband may be. Models in hiding count as close and may be hit. A hit reaches a model in cover only if the target was in cover.

rules.summary: One extra attack at Strength 3 in the first round
rules.text: It may be fired in the first round of combat, as a pistol: one extra attack at the wielder's Weapon Skill, resolved at Strength 3. If that attack hits and is not parried, 1D3 models in base contact with the firer are hit at Strength 3 as well, the closest first, his own warband among them. This is not shooting into combat, so the shots are not randomised, and no model takes more than one hit for one shot (a Ricochet critical aside). Once fired in the first round it may not be fired again in that combat.

rules.name: Loading Time
rules.text: Reloading always takes a whole turn, whatever skills the firer has, and he may fire no weapon other than a pistol while he reloads.

rules.name: Unbraced
rules.text: It is never bought as a brace, and a hero may own only one. A firer with the Pistolier skill may fire it together with one pistol of another type.

rules.name: Single Shot
rules.text: It holds one shot, and may not be used again for the rest of the battle.

rules.name: Tiny
rules.text: One Pocket Pistol does not count towards the missile weapons a hero may carry, and a model may carry two.

rules.name: Hidden
rules.text: The hero carries it even in a scenario that deprives heroes of their weapons. Whenever he is captured, by an injury roll, a bounty hunter, the Pressganger skill or anything else, he escapes unharmed with all his equipment on a 4+. Carrying two still gives one roll.

rules.name: Pistol-Like
rules.text: Out of combat it works as a Duelling Pistol, with the rules for pistol fire, Accuracy, Prepare shot and its save modifier.
In close combat a model wielding a Sword Pistol gains one parry a turn, as with a sword.

rules.name: Intricate
rules.text: If a parry with the Sword Pistol rolls a natural 1, it counts as a plain sword for the rest of the battle: it may no longer fire out of combat and loses Balanced and Blasting Charge.

rules.name: Balanced
rules.text: In the first round of close combat every attack with the Sword Pistol is at +1 to hit.

rules.name: Blasting Charge
rules.text: The first hit it deals in the first round of close combat deals, besides the hit at the user's Strength, an extra attack at Strength 4 with a further -1 to the enemy's armour save. After the first round it counts as a sword with the Intricate rule. The Blasting Charge may be used at the beginning of each new combat.

rules.name: Fresh Powder
rules.text: A hero whose gunpowder has become wet (walking through water, rain) may use the horn for fresh powder, enough for every powder weapon he carries for the rest of the battle, or until he becomes wet again. Used while he is still wet (standing in deep water, in a continuous storm) the powder is good for one turn only. If he was using Superior Blackpowder this game, the horn holds superior powder too. A model may carry several horns, each used once per game.

rules.name: A case of grog
rules.text: A case holds doses for 1D6 warriors and may be drunk at the start of a game. A henchmen group may drink only if there is enough for every member, or none of them may. Everyone who drinks passes automatically every Leadership test he must take, and is at -1 Weapon Skill and -1 Ballistic Skill. A leader who drinks does not pass rout tests automatically, and no warrior may use his Leadership that game. Elves may not drink it, and it has no effect on a model immune to poison.

rules.name: Deployment
rules.text: A raft is placed when you deploy, against the water nearest your deployment zone, or anywhere within your deployment zone on land. Two models may carry it at their base movement, with no running.

rules.name: Snare
rules.text: Once per game, instead of shooting a missile weapon, the net may be thrown in the shooting phase. Treat it as a missile weapon in every respect, with a range of 8", and use the model's Ballistic Skill to hit, with no penalty for moving or for range. A model it hits rolls a D6 at once: equal to or under his Strength he breaks free; over it he may not move, shoot or cast spells in his next turn, though he is not otherwise affected. Either way the net is used for that game.

rules.name: Made to Last
rules.text: Unlike other nets, a Norlander Net is always retrieved after the battle and may be used again, once per game. A hero may carry only one in a game.

rules.name: Fit for an admiral
rules.text: Only the warband's leader may wear it. The range of his Leadership is 3" further and he has +1 when searching for rare items. He may wear no helmet while he wears it. If he is taken out of action, roll a D6: on a 1-3 the opponent who took him out takes the hat (with several players, a random opponent where that is unclear).

rules.name: Whittled luck
rules.text: Once per game, during any of his turns, a hero using the charm gives one of his dice rolls in each phase +1 or -1: one in Recovery, one in Movement, one in Shooting and one in Combat. The effects last until the end of that turn. The warband's leader may use it on a rout test.

rules.name: Silvered
rules.text: Attacks with these count as magical against true undead, daemons and other mystical creatures, in shooting and in close combat, so they negate an unmodified mystical save, Ethereal among them, but not Dodge or Step Aside. There is enough for one game. Decide when they are bought or found whether they are arrows or bullets; they stay that until they are used or discarded.

rules.name: Jolly Roger
rules.text: One per warband, carried by any Hero. Any Pirate within 12" of the Jolly Roger never counts as All Alone.

rules.name: 'Friendly' Flag
rules.text: After set-up the warband may advance a further 6" in. The High Elf Lothern Sea Guard may not use it.

rules.name: Hourglass
rules.text: Roll D6+6. On the turn of that number every opposing warband that has suffered at least one notable casualty (a Swabbie does not count) is at its Rout level.

rules.name: Nation's Colors
rules.text: While the warband's leader, or the model acting as leader, is within 12" of the banner, he passes automatically the first rout check he must take. The next turn he may ignore a rout check on a 4+, and the turn after on a 6+. None of these dice may be re-rolled by any means. If he carries a Holy Relic and the first Leadership test he must take is a rout check, the Nation's Colors and the relic are both spent at once, and the Colors still ignore the next test on a 4+ and then on a 6+. A Navy warband may field no other flag. Its cost is the leader's.

rules.name: Quarantine Flag
rules.text: When an enemy takes the bearer out of action in close combat, the model that inflicted the injury takes a Toughness test: roll a D6, and if the result is higher than his Toughness he suffers an automatic wound; a 6 always wounds. Undead and possessed models never take this test. Only the Carnival of Chaos and members of Clan Pestilens may take this flag.

rules.name: Red Flag
rules.text: Every member of the warband within 6" of the banner causes fear. Only a warband that can take prisoners may fly it, and in any game you bring it you may take no prisoners afterwards.

flags.what: The skill table's ticks are glyphs the text layer drops: the table was read from p3's image. The Pirate column is ticked for the Captain, the Mate and the Cabin Boy.

The Swabbie Equipment list's Missile Weapons (Belaying Pin 3 gc, Bow 10 gc) and Armour (Buckler 5 gc, Toughened leathers 5 gc) are printed at the top of the right column, continuing the left column; read that way, as the Araby Smugglers' and Slayer Pirates' pages are laid out the same.
A Pirate warband needs at least 3 models: our templates hold no minimum, so it is not imported. No henchmen group sizes and no maximum profile are printed: the crew takes our Human race.
Swabbies have no hire price (they are captured, not hired): their cost is 0 gc.
The Swivel Gun's line is 65 gc, Rare 8, one per warband; our Swivel Gun is 65 gc, Rare 8 already, so the line only carries the limit.
The Cat O' Nine Tails, Boat Hook, Belaying Pin, Swivel Gun and its Ball, Chain and Grape Shot are all ours, at the list's prices; the PDF prints no rules for them.

The four 'Old' Pirate Skills are our Sea Shanty Singer, Cutlass Master, Booming Voice and Hardy Constitution, the same words; they are the Sartosan Pirates' own group here, while our Pirates group (the 1b Pirate warband's) holds them with Sea Legs and Swashbuckler besides.

The Pirate column is the Pirate Skills list of the Sartosa campaign rules (Sartosa Skills, Hired Swords and Dramatis Personae, p1-2), not this PDF: it is the shared Sartosa Pirate Skills group, declared in sartosan-pirates.json and named by each hero who ticks it.

The Sartosa campaign rules' Equipment PDF (p10) prints one trading list for the whole setting. William, 11 Nov 2026 (decision 20): it goes in as price rows for the Sartosa warband types, and our own prices and rarities never change. Each row below is one the setting's shop prices differently from ours; the list is declared here once, for all twelve Sartosa warband types, and a warband's own list price still wins for that warband. Throwing Axes get no row: they are our Throwing Knives/Stars/Axes, 15 gc Rare 5 for everyone already (William, 11 Nov 2026).

The setting's Equipment PDF prints eighteen items our catalogue lacks: they are stubs with the rules and prices it prints, one row for the setting's twelve warband types (William, 11 Nov 2026: "add them in as stubs if you dont have the rules for them yet, we will populate later but good to know they exist"). The Quarantine Flag is 40+2D6 on the trading chart and 30+2D6 in its entry: the entry's, as William settled for the Horn of the Wild Hunt. Each of the six Banners carries the shared Pirate Banner rule and its own. The Greatcoat (10 gc, Common) is our Rain Coat, "Based on 'Raincoat' from Border Town Burning" and the same price, so it is no new item: it is a tag on ours, and the PDF adds that it may be worn over armour without penalty but not with a cloak, and does not keep powder dry when walking through water. The Powder Monkey has no rules in either PDF read.

sharedSkillGroup.name: Sartosa Pirate Skills
sharedSkillGroup.note: A hero may know only one of these at a time; Pistol Expertise doesn't count towards that limit. For a promoted henchman it takes up no skill list.

skills.name: Pistol Expertise
skills.description: The Hero may use any pistol he finds or buys. A non-Skaven model may not buy a Warplock Pistol, but may use one he has taken. In hand-to-hand combat, whenever an opponent in base contact is knocked down or stunned, he reloads his pistols. This skill does not count towards the one Pirate skill a hero may know, so he may learn another beside it.

skills.name: Riposte
skills.description: When the Hero parries an attack he makes one extra attack at once, resolved before the attacker's other attacks.

skills.name: Impenetrable Defense
skills.description: When armed with two swords or other parrying weapons, the warrior gains a parry and a re-roll, as if he were armed with a sword and a buckler.

skills.name: Prince of Cats
skills.description: When armed with a Cat O' Nine Tails or a Whip, the Hero makes all his base attacks before a charger, not only the whipcrack attack. Attacks from an additional hand weapon are not included unless it is another whip or cat.

skills.name: Powder Refiner
skills.description: If the Hero does not search for rare items or dramatis personae, he makes 1D3-1 batches of Superior Blackpowder, so he may make none. They must be used in the next battle and may not be sold.

skills.name: Quick as a Monkey
skills.description: The Hero may run or charge while climbing.

skills.name: Snapshot
skills.description: A model armed with a pistol with a shot prepared may fire it in the first round of a hand-to-hand combat, resolved first, before any blows are struck. The shot is at a further -2 to hit and uses his Ballistic Skill. It is in addition to his close combat attacks. He may make only one Snapshot in a combat, and gains no extra attack from a second weapon in that first round.

skills.name: Dirty Fighter
skills.description: The Hero counts +2 Initiative for working out the order of attacks in close combat.

skills.name: Swing
skills.description: The Hero may declare a diving charge against a model within 2D6" of a building, rather than 2". Roll the distance after the charge is declared. He may use this skill only while he owns a Rope & Hook.

skills.name: Smell of Treasure
skills.description: When a Hero of the warband finds a Treasure Map or a Mordheim Map on his rarity roll, you may roll to see which result the map is before deciding to buy it. If you do not buy it you pay nothing, but that Hero's rarity roll is spent for this post-battle sequence. It works on a map any Hero finds, as long as the Hero with this skill was not taken out of action in the last battle.

skills.name: Helmsmen
skills.description: Any boat or raft the Hero travels in may move up to 3" further each turn.

skills.name: Festooned with Pistols
skills.description: The Hero may carry any number of braces of pistols. He may carry only one missile weapon that is not a pistol, and still reloads only one barrel a turn; with Pistolier he may instead fire and reload a barrel in the same turn.

skills.name: Looting the Dead
skills.description: When rolling for warriors taken out of action at the end of a battle, roll a D6 for each warrior who is to be removed from his roster and is not taken as a Swabbie or Crew. On a 4+ the looter takes all of that warrior's equipment and the warband keeps it. A warrior may be looted only once, but several Looters give several chances. Warriors of any warband in the game may be looted, your own among them.

skills.name: Novice Press-ganger
skills.description: The warband's leader only. The warband may capture Swabbies and Crew, as a Pirate warband does. A Crew mate joins a henchmen group costing 25 gold crowns or less; if the warband has none, he joins its cheapest group that is not animals and the player pays the difference in cost (into a 30 gc group, 5 gc). A Swabbie joins any group that is not animals costing 15 gold crowns or less, or failing that has a human henchman's profile. Where a fitting kind of Swabbie exists for the warband, it may recruit that instead.

skills.name: Master Press-ganger
skills.description: The warband's leader only. When a henchman the warband takes out of action dies (1-2 on his injury roll), the warband may try to recruit him as a Swabbie or Crew on a 2+ instead of 4+. When an enemy the warband took out of action dies (11-15 on the Serious Injury chart), on a D6 roll of 4+ he is captured instead, to be ransomed or made to join the crew.

itemRules.name: Pirate Banner
itemRules.summary: One flag per warband; one hand, no two-handed weapons
itemRules.text: A pirate warband may carry one pirate flag. Carrying it takes up one hand, so its bearer may carry or use no two-handed weapon during the game. A Swabbie gains no benefit from a Pirate Banner. A good warband (the Sisters of Sigmar, the Witch Hunters, the Lothern Sea Patrol) may carry only the Nation's Colors.
